data.body:
EPIC PLAN REVIEW #2 -> BLOCK, but 4 blocking -> 1. The three truncated-AC blockers and the pinned-file blocker are RESOLVED.
REMAINING BLOCKER (G6, impact 0.8) is the SAME drift I had already found independently via the failed mutation and filed as bug fe15 — the reviewer's evidence matches mine exactly (jira_fields.py:35-41,62-70 vs outbound_fields.py:84-104; backend.py map_fields_to_remote reads the outbound_fields copies). Independent corroboration, not a new problem.
REMEDIATION #2: the fix hinges on a distinction the plan had conflated — 'location-pinned' means the file CANNOT CHANGE PATH, not that it cannot be EDITED. The loader resolves by path and ignores contents, so replacing a dict literal inside the pinned outbound_fields.py with an import from jira_family/ is safe. Updated the epic and J2 to make adapters/jira_family/ the SOLE definition site for the status/priority maps: BOTH existing literals are deleted and replaced by imports (jira_fields.py relocates; outbound_fields.py stays at its path with edited contents). Added ACs: exactly one dict literal per map engine-wide (grep-verified), and observable behavior unchanged for both the ACLI and Backend-port callers. Clarified the pinned-path AC to forbid renames only, not edits. Scoped the 'deleted'-key drift decision OUT to bug fe15 so J2 stays behavior-preserving.
